headline: Rain and breezy winds tonight and Sunday, showers Monday, then another wet system Wednesday.
summary: A storm off the coast is moving in and will drift slowly south and east through Monday morning. Rain arrives tonight, and a cold front (the leading edge of cooler air) brings heavier rain overnight, mostly along the coast and Olympic Peninsula. Breezy south winds gust to 20 to 35 mph in many areas. Showers linger into Monday before moving east late in the day, though the track of the ground-level storm center (the surface low) is uncertain and could extend the rain. Highs stay near normal, in the mid to upper 50s. Tuesday should be mostly light and focused south of the region, and a stronger system arrives Wednesday with widespread rain. Showery, unsettled weather continues Thursday through Saturday.
changes: Compared with the earlier afternoon discussion, forecasters added rain totals and wind gusts, and expanded the gale and small craft warnings for the coastal waters. By evening, they were more specific about the Monday storm track, naming the models that disagree and noting that the upper-level low's path is more settled.
